sentences.text: Solicitor Sophie Grant attended the meeting with client Lee Whitfield.
The purpose of the meeting was to discuss the client's housing situation, including rent arrears and court proceedings.
Client Lee Whitfield lost his job at a depot in January.
The client's Universal Credit housing element took a long time to process, and the housing element went wrong, leading to rent arrears.
The rent arrears amount is £3,850, for three to four months.
The client received court papers for a possession claim on rent arrears grounds (grounds 8, 10, and 11) by Ashcroft Lettings.
The hearing is scheduled for the 9th of December at Harbridge County Court.
The property is a private rental property.
The client lives alone with a cat.
The client offered £50 per month in September to settle the arrears, which the landlord rejected.
The client has a text message recording the offer of £50 per month, which is stored on their phone.
The client reported damp in the bedroom, with black mould on the wall.
The client has photographs of the damp in the bedroom.
The client has outstanding debts including council tax (bailiffs letter sent), a credit card debt of approximately £2,000, and electric bill on a meter.
The client has no support from family or friends, with only a brother in Doncaster who does not communicate regularly.
The client visited his GP in March after receiving the first rent arrears letter.
The client took an overdose of 16 paracetamol in March after receiving the first rent arrears letter.
The client's neighbour found him and called an ambulance, and he was admitted overnight to hospital.
After hospital admission, a nurse contacted the client a couple of times, then stopped contacting.
The client has not hurt himself since March.
The client thought about ending his life on Sunday night, this week, before the court date.
The client is currently safe and stable today.
The client stated that talking about the suicidal thoughts helped him feel a bit better.
The client reported that he had previously submitted issues with the housing costs to the Universal Credit journal twice, but received no response.
The solicitor requires the following documents: tenancy agreement, rent statement, Universal Credit statements since January, and damp photos.
The solicitor advised the client that the arrears are due to the housing element going wrong, and that the damp may be a valid counterclaim to reduce the arrears.
The solicitor will file a defence and a counterclaim for damp issues.
The solicitor will request the court to adjourn if more time is needed to resolve the Universal Credit issue.
The solicitor will refer the client to the Citizens Advice debt team for a breathing space (60-day period during which creditors do not chase the client).
The solicitor will write to Universal Credit to support the defence of the housing claim.
